---
title: "Handling Missing Data"
output: html_notebook
---

Pre-requisites of handling missing data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
library(naniar)
library(gtExtras)
```

Datasets to use

```{r}
View(airquality)
data(starwars)
```

Displaying missingness of data

```{r}
miss_var_summary(airquality) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title="Missingness of a variable")
```

Displaying only the null values

```{r}
airquality %>% 
  filter(!complete.cases(.)) %>% 
  head(10) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title = "Rows that have missing data")
```

Visualizing missing data

```{r}
vis_miss(airquality)

```

Relationship to one variable

```{r}
airquality %>% 
  mutate(Missing_Ozone = factor(is.na(Ozone),
                                levels=c("True","False"),
                                labels=c("Missing","Not Missing"))) %>%
           ggplot(aes(x=airquality$Wind),fill=Missing_Ozone)+
           geom_histogram(position = "stack")+
           labs(title="Distribution of Wind Speeds for Missing Vs Not Missing")+
           theme_classic()

```

To display the distribution of the missing values

```{r}
airquality %>% 
  select(Ozone,Solar.R,Wind,Temp) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Wind,y=Temp,size=Solar.R,color=is.na(Ozone)))+
  geom_point(alpha=0.7)+
  facet_wrap(~is.na(Ozone))+
  labs(title = "Distribution of missing data")
```

Handling Missing Values

1.  Dropping Missing Values where by we will see the observations that we are going to remove

```{r}
starwars %>%
  select(name,mass,height,hair_color) %>% 
  head(15) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title="Starwars Characters") %>% 
  gt_highlight_rows(rows=is.na(mass),
                    fill="steelblue") %>% 
  gt_highlight_rows(rows=is.na(hair_color),
                    fill="lightpink")
```

To now remove the missing value in the mass variable

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name,mass,height,hair_color) %>% 
  drop_na(mass) %>% 
  head(20) %>% 
  gt() %>% 
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title="Starwars Characters")
  

```

2.  Changing the missing values

    Here first we will generate a table that has the missing values for hair_color

    ```{r}
    starwars %>% 
      select(name,hair_color,species) %>% 
      filter(species=="Droid") %>% 
      head(5) %>% 
      gt() %>% 
      gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
      tab_header(title="Starwars Characters")
    ```

Now changing the hair color whenever its NA to none

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name,hair_color,species) %>% 
  filter(species=="Droid") %>% 
  mutate(hair_color=case_when(
    is.na(hair_color)&
      species=="Droid"~"none",
    TRUE ~hair_color
  )) %>% 
  gt() %>%
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title="Starwars")
    

```

3.  Imputation

    Here we change the missing values to a median or to the mean value of the observations

    First we will display the missing values in the height variable

    ```{r}
    starwars %>%
      select(name,height) %>% 
      filter(is.na(height)) %>%
      gt() %>% 
      gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
      tab_header(title="Starwars Characters")
      
    ```

Replacing the missing value with the true Median value of the observations

```{r}
starwars %>% 
  select(name,height) %>% 
  mutate(height = case_when(
    is.na(height) ~ median(height,rm.na=TRUE),
    TRUE ~ height
  )) %>%
  gt() %>%
  gt_theme_guardian() %>% 
  tab_header(title="Starwars Characters ")
```
